name: Standing Cable Pullover with Rope
description: The standing cable pullover with a rope attachment allows the hands to pronate and spread at the bottom of the movement, creating a more natural wrist path and greater lat contraction than a straight bar pullover. The rope version is performed facing a high cable with the torso bent slightly forward, drawing the rope from overhead to the thighs in a large arc while maintaining straight elbows.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a high cable pulley. Attach a rope. Grasp the rope and step back, bending forward slightly at the hips. Arms extended overhead toward the pulley.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the cable to the highest position. Bend forward 20-30 degrees at the hips to allow a fuller arc. Moderate weight.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended overhead, lats stretched.
Step 2: Pull the rope down in a broad arc, keeping elbows straight.
Step 3: As the rope reaches hip level, spread the hands apart slightly.
Step 4: At the bottom, squeeze the lats hard for 1 second.
Step 5: Return under control — the stretch at the top is as important as the contraction.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull. Inhale returning overhead.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — this becomes a pulldown, not a pullover
Standing too upright — a slight forward lean increases the range and lat emphasis
safety_considerations: Keep the core braced — a bent-over position with heavy loads stresses the lower back
The shoulder must be healthy to load the overhead stretched position
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full overhead stretch to thigh contact at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Spread the rope apart at the bottom to maximize lat contraction
Think of pulling your armpits to your hips
Long arms throughout — no elbow bend
